name: usb-hub-escapes
prompt: USB-C in, four USB 2.0 ports out, RP2040 doing the control side. JLCPCB four layer. The differential pairs need to stay matched and I want the escapes out of the RP2040 done in code so I can regenerate them when the pinout moves.

inputs.parts: jitxexamples.components.mcus.raspberry_pi_RP2040 for the controller. Use a real USB-C receptacle and downstream connectors from jitxexamples.components.connectors where one fits, or a clearly labelled placeholder with its pad geometry stated.
inputs.notes: The brief gives no geometry and no rule list on purpose. Pad pitch, escape width, channel width and pair spacing all have to come from queried landpattern copper, a fabrication row, or a routing structure, and the source has to answer the question it is used for.
inputs.environment: Commands run from the repository root with an interpreter that has jitx installed and a reachable runtime.

expected_output: Layout code that authors the escapes and the pair routing through control points rather than by hand, a design that builds, and checks that read the captured design back. Differential legs must be shown to have kept their polarity and their pairing, not merely to exist.

assertions.text: escapes are authored with control points rather than as free routes, with the transition split at a RoutePoint and the tag carried on the segment rather than on the net
each differential pair realizes two traces, and each leg is resolved to its own net so polarity is established rather than assumed from drawing order
the circuit that owns each route is the common ancestor of its endpoints, and a route whose endpoints sit in sibling circuits is placed accordingly rather than on whichever circuit was convenient
every declared rule is witnessed by a check, reported through rule_coverage with unwitnessed rules named rather than passed over
clearance_relaxations is run and reports no relaxation, or names the relaxation and how it was resolved
no check passes on an empty selection: a gate that measured nothing fails
the checker library the skill routes to is importable in the environment used

future_cases: A pinout change re-run, to establish that regenerating the escapes from code actually survives the pins moving, which is the reason the engineer asked for code in the first place.
